svg.title: Software Supply Chain Guardian — architecture
svg.desc: Six-step flow: GitHub and dashboard inputs; deterministic scan and score; evidence-based AI investigation; computed fixes and human approval; isolated Docker validation; dashboard and reports. Shared evidence storage and all ten M0–M9 milestones. Official logos embedded from publishers.

g.text: BOSCH BGSW / SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN GUARDIAN
From a pull request to an evidence-backed decision
Or: dashboard / CLI · Git URL · ZIP · local repo
PR code is read; the trigger does not execute it.
OSV / Grype + 14 supply-chain detectors + CI checks
KEV · EPSS · SSVC · priority · confidence · exposure
Rules decide: ALLOW / REVIEW / BLOCK / INCOMPLETE
Stored evidence packets; citations checked by code
Token budget + response cache + usage ledger
AI review is optional; rules verdict stays unchanged.
Ordered rules → one combined patch → SHA-256
Fixer explains the computed plan; code checks claims
Bound to commits, patch, policy and validation profile
Approved baseline vs candidate in disposable containers
Install → build → security test → unit → integration
Artifact SBOM + source rescan → deterministic gate
Approval checked first · non-root · registry-only network
Before / after risk · remaining risk · audit trail
SQLite index + SHA-256 blobs · run JSON files · patches · hash-linked audit log · AI cache + token ledger
M0 trust checks apply throughout. M9 documents the system. Diagram shows implemented paths, not universal deployment readiness.
¹ GitHub publishing requires token permissions. Full validation requires human approval and a matching profile; app-image build is outside the current profile.
Solid arrows: main flow · Dashed lines: shared persistence · Official logos retain their original colors; tool names identify each integration.
